column1: In Data API builder (DAB), define the Product API entity under the top-level {{c1::entities}} section.
column2:
An entity names the database object that DAB exposes and controls how clients access it.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0, use {{c1::alias}} in a fields array entry to give a SQL column a different API name.
column2:
For example, pair name: UnitPrice with alias: price so clients use price without a SQL schema change.
Review source

column1: To change only Product's DAB REST route from /api/Product to /api/products, set its {{c1::rest.path}} to /products.
column2:
The entity route changes, but the global /api prefix and the GraphQL names stay the same.
Review source

column1: To set both singular and plural names for one DAB entity in GraphQL, use {{c1::graphql.type}}.
column2:
For example, use product as the singular name and products as the plural name in the GraphQL schema.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0, REST caching needs global runtime.cache.enabled and per-entity {{c1::cache.enabled}} set to true.
column2:
The global setting turns on caching for the service, and the entity setting opts that entity in.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0, the entity cache setting {{c1::ttl-seconds}} sets how long a REST cache entry can live.
column2:
Set it under the entity's cache object to override the global lifetime in seconds.
Review source

column1: DAB 2.0's built-in in-memory response cache applies only to {{c1::REST}} endpoints.
column2:
The product reference places cache settings under the entity's cache object, not under its graphql object as shown in the training unit.
Review source

column1: To request at most 10 rows per page in DAB REST, use {{c1::$first}}=10.
column2:
A page is one batch of results, which can contain fewer rows than requested if fewer rows match.
Review source

column1: In DAB REST, {{c1::$after}} carries the token that resumes a query after the previous page.
column2:
Use the token returned in nextLink as-is because it marks where the last page ended.
Review source

column1: To request at most 10 rows per page in DAB GraphQL, use the argument {{c1::first}}: 10.
column2:
For example, products(first: 10) limits one page without changing which products match.
Review source

column1: In DAB GraphQL, pass the previous page's endCursor as the next request's {{c1::after}} argument.
column2:
A cursor marks where the last page ended, so reuse DAB's value without editing it.
Review source

column1: In DAB GraphQL, request {{c1::hasNextPage}} to find out whether more rows remain after this page.
column2:
If the field is true, use endCursor to fetch the next page.
Review source

column1: In DAB REST, use {{c1::$filter}} to return only rows that match a condition.
column2:
For example, $filter=price gt 100 includes prices above 100 and excludes prices equal to 100.
Review source

column1: In DAB GraphQL, use the {{c1::filter}} argument to pass conditions as an object.
column2:
For example, filter: { price: { gt: 100 } } restricts which products the query returns.
Review source

column1: In a DAB GraphQL filter, {{c1::contains}} matches text anywhere inside a string field.
column2:
For example, contains: "SQL" can match both SQL Basics and Learning SQL Today.
Review source

column1: For a DAB GraphQL relationship from a product to its category, set cardinality to {{c1::one}}.
column2:
Read cardinality from the current entity to the target, so one product can point to at most one category.
Review source

column1: In a DAB GraphQL relationship, set {{c1::target.entity}} to the name of the related API entity.
column2:
For example, a product relationship points to the Category entity, not directly to the dbo.Categories table.
Review source

column1: To create a row at a DAB REST table's collection URL, use the HTTP method {{c1::POST}}.
column2:
For example, send the new product's fields to POST /api/Product if the caller has create permission.
Review source

column1: In DAB 2.0, per-entity rest.methods takes an array of HTTP method names and applies only to {{c1::stored-procedure}} sources.
column2:
For example, use ["POST"] for a procedure rather than the Boolean method object shown for a table in the training unit.
Review source

column1: In DAB, {{c1::runtime.graphql.allow-introspection}} controls whether clients can ask for the GraphQL schema.
column2:
Introspection lets clients discover available fields and operations, but the setting does not grant data access.
Review source

column1: In DAB, {{c1::runtime.graphql.depth-limit}} caps how deeply GraphQL queries can nest fields.
column2:
A depth cap can reject queries that follow too many levels of related entities.
Review source

column1: For a DAB stored procedure, the entity setting {{c1::graphql.operation}} places its execute field under Query or Mutation.
column2:
This changes where clients find the procedure in the schema, not what the procedure does.
Review source
